newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Aberfoyle sees higher demand for zinc.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Aberfoyle sees higher demand for zinc.

text.p: Base metal miner Aberfoyle Ltd said on Thursday it expected world demand for zinc to improve and oustrip supply in 1997, resulting in a reduction of world stocks to more acceptable levels.

"As stocks decline we expect to see improved zinc prices and we expect the market for zinc concentrates to remain relatively tight throughout 1997," the company's chairman Max Richards told the company's annual meeting in Melbourne.
Richards said Aberfoyle expected the price of lead to remain strong in 1997 even though the mine output of lead was increasing and the market was seen better supplied in 1997.
Richards said the price of copper would become more important for Aberfoyle following the company's decision to expand its Gunpowder copper mine in Queensland.

"With significant new (world) production, including Gunpowder, planned or being developed, it is unlikely that growing demand will exceed this increased capacity and we do not expect any substantial increase in copper price in the medium term," he said.
An improvement in metal prices and/or a lower exchange rate would be required for Aberfoyle to meet or exceed its 1996 profit, Richards said.

Aberfoyle's net profit fell 44 percent to A$8.88 million in the year to June 30, 1996 from A$15.91 million in the previous year. The company's operating profit fell to A$15.9 million from A$27.25 million.
Richards said the company was still looking at potential acquisitions with its search aimed at larger purchases than those it had achieved to date.
"With a strong balance sheet and high cash flows from Hellyer (base metal mine in Tasmania), the company is well positioned to take advantage of opportunities," Richards said.
